glosses: Marquer une carte d’un signe particulier ou guidon, pour tricher.

examples.text: Il a guidonné les as.

glosses: Effectuer des mouvements incontrôlables (en parlant du guidon d'une moto ou d’un vélo).

examples.text: Pour essayer d’éviter à une moto de guidonner, la pose d'un amortisseur de direction est conseillée surtout sur une hyper-sportive.

translations.source_sense_description: (Cyclisme, Motocyclisme) Effectuer des mouvements incontrôlables (en parlant du guidon d'une moto ou d’un vélo).

glosses: A dance move involving thrusting the shoulders back and forth alternately.
A dance that was popular in the 1920s.

examples.text: The tango, the Texas Tommy, Walking the Dog, the one step, the fox trot, the shimmy, and all their out-growths, had their origin in the palaces of lust on the Barbary Coast of San Francisco.

glosses: An abnormal vibration, especially in the wheels of a vehicle.
To perform a shimmy (dance movement involving thrusting the shoulders back and forth alternately).

examples.text: She wondered would he think her awful, and try to get fresh if she shimmied. Fellows often did. But he was so cute. And a girl had to something about that, and if she didn't shimmy, she might do something worse.

glosses: To climb something (e.g. a pole) gradually (e.g. using alternately one's arms then one's legs).

examples.text: He shimmied up the flagpole.
The static made her dress shimmy up her leg.

glosses: To vibrate abnormally, as a broken wheel.

examples.text: They came in among earth-moving machines, a total absence of trees, the usual hieratic geometry, and eventually, shimmying for the sand roads, down in a helix to a sculptured body of water named Lake Inverarity.

glosses: To shake the body as if dancing the shimmy.
To move across a narrow ledge, either by hanging from it or by strafing on it along the wall.

examples.text: Jump up to the ledge on your right and shimmy around the corner.
Climb on top of the room and drop down to shimmy along its back ledge.

examples.text: The fat man walked down the street with a wobble.
That should have been that, but Hart caught a dose of the Hennessey wobbles and spilled Adlene Guedioura's long-range shot.
There was a wobble on her high notes.

glosses: A low-frequency oscillation sometimes used in dubstep.

examples.text: “I Knew You Were Trouble,” one of the year’s great pop songs, begins like a sock-hop anthem, with jaunty guitars. A dubstep wobble arrives about halfway through like a wrecking ball, changing the course not just of the song but also of Ms. Swift’s career.

glosses: A variation in the third nucleotide of a codon that codes for a specific aminoacid.
To move with an uneven or rocking motion, or unsteadily to and fro.

examples.text: the Earth wobbles slowly on its axis
the jelly wobbled on the plate
The apparition wobbled in front of Arthur's eyes, though the truth of the matter is probably that Arthur's eyes were wobbling in front of the apparition. His mouth wobbled as well.

Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually zero in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent weeks but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new sources of return.
The soprano's voice wobbled alarmingly.
I'm wobbling between the Liberals and the Greens.
The boy wobbled the girl's bike.

He said: “This front wheel wobbles.”
I said: “It doesn’t if you don’t wobble it.” It didn’t wobble, as a matter of fact—nothing worth calling a wobble.
